title: GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C for FY 2025-26: Due 31 December 2026 – What to Check
excerpt: The GST annual return for FY 2025-26 is due on 31 December 2026. Who must file GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C, what to reconcile first, the 30 November ITC cut-off and the late fee.
body:
The GST annual return for FY 2025-26 is due on **31 December 2026**. That covers GSTR-9, the annual return, and GSTR-9C, the reconciliation statement. The GST portal opened filing for FY 2025-26 in October 2026. With about five weeks left, this is a good time to start reconciling your books with your GST returns.

## Who has to file GSTR-9

The requirement depends on your **aggregate turnover** for FY 2025-26. That is the turnover of all GST registrations under the same PAN, added together.

- **Up to ₹2 crore**: GSTR-9 is not required.
- **Above ₹2 crore**: GSTR-9 must be filed.
- **Above ₹5 crore**: you also file GSTR-9C, which reconciles the turnover and tax in your audited financial statements with what you reported in GSTR-9.

GSTR-9C is now **self-certified** by the taxpayer, so a chartered accountant no longer has to sign it. You still need audited or final accounts to prepare it properly.

## What you need before you start

Before the GSTR-9 option appears on the portal, every **GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B for FY 2025-26** has to be filed. If any month or quarter is pending, file it first. Late fees and interest apply to those returns.

Keep these ready:

- Sales and purchase registers for April 2025 to March 2026
- All GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B returns filed for the year
- GSTR-2B statements, because the input tax credit (ITC) figure in Table 8A is built from GSTR-2B
- Credit notes, debit notes and amendments, including those reported after March 2026
- An HSN-wise summary of sales
- The trial balance, and for GSTR-9C, the audited financial statements

## Points to watch for FY 2025-26

**Two rate structures in one year.** GST rates on many goods and services changed from **22 September 2025**. Sales of the same HSN code before and after that date may have been taxed at different rates. In the HSN summary in Table 17, you may need separate rows for each rate. Businesses with turnover above ₹5 crore report 6-digit HSN codes. Smaller businesses report 4 digits.

**ITC reconciliation.** Compare the ITC you claimed in GSTR-3B with the GSTR-2B figure in Table 8A. Explain any large difference, such as missing supplier invoices, ITC you reversed, or ITC you reclaimed. ITC of the previous year that you claimed in this year is shown separately, as is ITC on imports.

**Last date for FY 2025-26 ITC.** Under section 16(4) of the CGST Act, ITC for invoices of FY 2025-26 can be claimed only up to **30 November 2026**, or the date you file the annual return if that is earlier. The same cut-off applies to correcting FY 2025-26 details in GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B. If you file GSTR-9 before 30 November, the window closes on your filing date.

**Some tables are optional.** A CBIC notification of October 2026 made the existing relaxations permanent from FY 2025-26 onwards. Several detailed tables in GSTR-9 and GSTR-9C stay optional, such as certain break-ups of exempt supplies and ITC, and the tables on refunds and demands. The core tables on outward supplies, ITC, tax paid and the HSN summary remain mandatory. Optional reporting does not remove a mismatch, so you should still reconcile the figures.

## No revision after filing

You cannot revise GSTR-9 once it is filed. If reconciliation shows that you paid less tax than you owed, pay the difference with interest through **Form DRC-03** before or while filing. Excess ITC claimed should also be reversed and paid back this way.

Underpayments found later can lead to notices and interest, so it pays to get the figures right the first time. Check them carefully before you submit.

## Late fee

If you miss 31 December, a late fee applies for each day of delay. The amounts below combine CGST and SGST:

- **Turnover up to ₹5 crore**: ₹50 per day, capped at 0.04% of turnover in the state
- **Turnover above ₹5 crore and up to ₹20 crore**: ₹100 per day, capped at 0.04% of turnover in the state
- **Turnover above ₹20 crore**: ₹200 per day, capped at 0.5% of turnover in the state

No extension has been announced as of now. Plan to file well before the last week of December, when the portal is usually busy.

## A simple timeline

- **By 30 November**: claim any remaining FY 2025-26 ITC and correct errors in GSTR-1 or GSTR-3B
- **First half of December**: finish reconciling purchases with GSTR-2B and sales with GSTR-1, and pay any shortfall through DRC-03
- **By 20 December**: file GSTR-9, then GSTR-9C if it applies to you
